beats.text: Wegener did not invent continental drift.
beats.note: Abraham Ortelius first put the idea forward in 1596, and Snider-Pellegrini and Reclus followed. Wegener was the first to use the phrase continental drift.
In Frankfurt. His book Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane followed in 1915.
He was known in his lifetime mainly for meteorology. Geologists treated him as an outsider.
Mesosaurus fossils turn up in Brazil and South Africa, and glacial sediments from the same period span the southern continents.

beats.context: Wegener's estimated drift speed, against about 2.5 cm a year as understood today. He also had no workable force, and calculations showed his centrifugal force was not enough.

beats.text: He did not live to see it settled.
beats.note: Wegener died in Greenland in November 1930. By 1967 plate tectonics had become axiomatic to modern geophysics.

beats.text: Right about the continents. Wrong about the cause.
